purpose: Agent-facing retrieval layer for southern Magallanes travel, protected areas and territorial connectivity.

chunks.title: Ruta de los Parques overview
chunks.summary: Ruta de los Parques sources describe a 2,800 km conservation and nature-travel corridor linking 17 national parks from Puerto Montt to Cabo de Hornos, integrating the Carretera Austral, Patagonian channels and the Ruta del Fin del Mundo.

chunks.title: National parks in the Magallanes section
chunks.summary: The Ruta de los Parques road map explicitly lists seven national parks in the Magallanes section: Bernardo O'Higgins, Kawesqar, Torres del Paine, Pali Aike, Alberto de Agostini, Yendegaia and Cabo de Hornos.

chunks.title: Yendegaia territorial and conservation context
chunks.summary: Yendegaia is a national park in the far south of Isla Grande de Tierra del Fuego, associated with the Beagle Channel and Cordillera Darwin. Current CONAF information places it in the communes of Timaukel and Cabo de Hornos.

chunks.title: Current Yendegaia access and visitor-service status
chunks.summary: As of 23 August 2026, CONAF describes maritime access from Puerto Williams/Puerto Navarino toward Bahia Yendegaia and a terrestrial approach via Ruta Y-85 to Lago Fagnano plus the Vicuna-Yendegaia penetration road. CONAF simultaneously states that the park has no visitor attention and no public-use infrastructure.
chunks.prohibited_inference: Do not promise a staffed entrance, public-use facilities, scheduled boat, or completed through-road connection to Puerto Williams.

chunks.title: Vicuna-Yendegaia road remains under construction
chunks.summary: Current 2026 Ejercito/CMT and MOP evidence shows the Vicuna-Yendegaia corridor remains under construction. The corridor must not be represented as a completed continuous public road to Puerto Williams.
chunks.prohibited_inference: Do not state that travelers can currently drive continuously from mainland Chile to Puerto Williams through this project.

chunks.title: TABSA Punta Arenas-Puerto Williams maritime connection
chunks.summary: TABSA currently publishes Punta Arenas-Puerto Williams as a maritime service and describes the crossing as approximately 32 hours. Departure dates, fares, vessel assignment and availability remain booking-sensitive and must be rechecked at answer time.

chunks.title: TABSA service scope includes Caleta 2 de Mayo
chunks.summary: TABSA's current Puerto Williams operations listing includes Punta Arenas, Puerto Williams, Puerto Toro and Caleta 2 de Mayo within its route/service scope. This confirms operator scope, not a guaranteed fixed-frequency itinerary to Caleta 2 de Mayo.

chunks.title: Current Cabo de Hornos visitor-access model
chunks.summary: Current CONAF information states that Parque Nacional Cabo de Hornos has public visitation subject to maritime access and advance planning; practical landing remains weather and operator dependent.

chunks.title: Current Alberto de Agostini visitor-access model
chunks.summary: Current CONAF information states that Parque Nacional Alberto de Agostini is accessed mainly by sea and has no administrative or public-use facilities inside the unit.

chunks.title: Current Primera Angostura crossing
chunks.summary: TABSA identifies Primera Angostura as the ferry crossing between Punta Delgada on the mainland and Bahia Azul on Tierra del Fuego. Operational status is dynamic and should be checked through TABSA immediately before travel.

chunks.title: Puerto Williams-Puerto Toro subsidized maritime service
chunks.summary: In August 2026 the Delegacion Presidencial Provincial de Antartica Chilena publishes sailings between Puerto Williams and Puerto Toro under a subsidized isolated-zone maritime service. It is explicitly not a tourism product and residents have priority.

chunks.title: San Sebastian border crossing
chunks.summary: Unidad de Pasos Fronterizos reported the San Sebastian complex operational in April 2026. It connects Chilean Tierra del Fuego with Argentina, is authorized for all vehicle types, and uses Ruta Y-71 on the Chilean side. Daily opening and conditions remain live operational information.
chunks.prohibited_inference: Do not promise opening hours or uninterrupted passage without a same-day official check.

chunks.title: Bellavista seasonal border crossing
chunks.summary: Bellavista is a seasonal border crossing in southern Tierra del Fuego. Official sources documented reopening on 1 October 2025 and reviewed its recent operation in May 2026. It must not be represented as a year-round crossing.

chunks.title: Porvenir as Tierra del Fuego service node
chunks.summary: Porvenir functions as the principal urban and service node of Chilean Tierra del Fuego. Municipal sources maintain tourism and service listings, while TABSA maintains maritime operations and fare material associated with Porvenir/Bahia Chilota. Timetables and vehicle space remain booking-sensitive.

chunks.title: Cerro Sombrero heritage and connectivity caution
chunks.summary: Cerro Sombrero is an interior Tierra del Fuego settlement with strong petroleum-industry heritage value. Older public documents show Porvenir-Cerro Sombrero bus services, but no sufficiently current timetable was verified for 2026; agents must not reuse old schedules as current.

chunks.title: Puerto Williams-Puerto Navarino road connection
chunks.summary: Puerto Navarino is connected to Puerto Williams by Ruta Y-905, approximately 54-56 km according to official sources. In 2026 Vialidad and the provincial delegation reported active road maintenance and weather-related deterioration on Navarino roads, so transit conditions should be rechecked before travel.

chunks.title: Puerto Navarino maritime-border infrastructure
chunks.summary: The provincial government reports a new ramp in Puerto Navarino that reactivated international maritime crossing capacity. This is infrastructure and connectivity evidence, not proof of a regular tourist passenger service or fixed timetable.
chunks.prohibited_inference: Do not sell or recommend a regular international ferry solely from the existence of the ramp.

chunks.title: Puerto Williams and Punta Arenas as southern park gateways
chunks.summary: The 2022 Ruta de los Parques brochure identifies Puerto Williams and Punta Arenas as gateway cities for southern protected-area access. This is route-context evidence, not proof that every current transport service or park access is available from both cities.

chunks.title: Ruta de los Parques responsible travel principles
chunks.summary: The route passport promotes low-impact travel: protect ecosystems, support local communities, respect traditions, reduce waste, do not feed wildlife, observe fauna from a distance, stay on marked trails, comply with fire bans and follow park-ranger instructions.
